long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in Highgate by a chemical-company owner and a university lecturer, Michael Sidney Sherwood attended Westminster School before graduating from Manchester. He joined Goldman Sachs, rose through debt syndication, became a partner in 1994 and later led European fixed income. As vice-chairman and co-chief executive of Goldman Sachs International, he oversaw business across EMEA and growth markets.

Sherwood retired from Goldman at the end of 2016. His documented late-career compensation included $21 million in one year, but that figure does not represent current earnings. He now serves as an independent non-executive director of Revolut and as a Credit Benchmark director and investor. Those personal interests and appointments are distinct from the assets, revenue and customer businesses of Goldman Sachs, Revolut and Credit Benchmark.
